summary: A forked chat can send a summary of its work back to its parent chat, as context only (no git merge). The backend builds the summary from the fork's history after its cursor (the fork point on the first send, then the end of the last delivered send): the turns as compact user and agent text, the files its mirrored diff cards name, its worktree and branch, and its last reply, capped at 16 KiB with the newest whole turns kept and the number left out stated. The user edits it in a confirm dialog (desktop: 'Send back to <parent>' in the fork banner, or /merge-back). The parent stores it as a pending card (one per fork; a new send replaces it) with Edit and Discard. The parent's next non-queued user turn carries every pending card to its agent, wrapped in <switchboard-fork-merge-back> so the agent reads it as Switchboard context on the user's behalf; the turn's commit transaction marks it delivered once, by revision, and the card becomes a delivered row above that message. A failed or ambiguous dispatch leaves it pending. State survives a restart (fork_merge_backs, fork_merge_back_cursors). Channels provider:merge-back-preview/send/edit/discard, the merge-back.row event and the fork_merge_back_v1 capability. Both phones render the card and the delivered row, and, when the backend advertises fork_merge_back_v1, offer Send back in a fork's banner (summary shown, editable, then sent) and Edit and Discard on a pending card in the parent. An older backend shows no action.

tests/unit/merge-back-service.test.ts against SQLite and the real AtomicUserTurnSubmission: pending card, edit (own parent only), discard; delivery with the next user turn exactly once (stored wrapped, shown as the user's words, delivered row just above the message); a refused turn leaves it pending and the next turn carries it; edit, discard and a second claim refused while a turn carries it; the next send carries only what is new; the preview token pins the range when the fork runs on; a second send replaces the pending card; a stale token after a delivery is refused; not a fork, a busy fork, an archived parent and empty text are refused; a pending card and the fork cursor survive a restart (serialized database).

tests/unit/merge-back-registry.test.ts against the real ProviderRegistry: the pending card rides on the next user turn once and its delivered event comes after the user message; a queued message does not carry it and the next normal one does; a failed provider call leaves it pending and editable.

notExercised: The desktop banner button, the dialog and the parent card were not seen in a running app and have no visual baseline (no visual screen shows a fork). The fork banner moved from inline styles to Tailwind utilities with the same values; no screen covers it, so pixel equality is unverified.
Not run against live Claude, Codex or OpenCode sessions: how each model treats the wrapped summary is untested; the adapters are fakes.
Files are read from the mirrored diff cards, so a file whose diff was too large to mirror (MIRRORED_FILE_DIFF_MAX_CHARS) is not listed.
The originless legacy SEND_TURN path (clients from before durable turn origins) does not carry a pending summary; it stays pending for the next modern send.
Phone Send back, Edit and Discard were not run on a device or against a live backend; only component, store and coordinator tests cover them.
